topic: Runtime surface parity across the seven runtimes: commands, skills, agents, goal and hooks

strategies: Iteration 1 uses a name-normalized mirror diff plus direct reads of the mirror generators; counted facts are recorded as contradicted/charter-corrected rather than inherited verbatim.

focus: Command census: authored 35 commands against six mirrors, exclusion rules, generators and --check coverage
noveltyJustification: First pass over a chartered surface; the counts were partly known, but the exclusion/native policy that produces them, the symlink-versus-copy mechanism split, the 35-versus-46 correction and the two unwired --check modes are all new.
keyQuestions: What is the exact per-runtime command matrix?
Is every count difference a deliberate exclusion rule or drift?
Which generator produces each mirror and does it have --check?
answeredQuestions: What is the exact per-runtime command matrix?
Is every count difference a deliberate exclusion rule or drift?
Which generator produces each mirror and does it have --check?

ruledOut.approach: Treat the 33-versus-35 mirror spread as drift to be repaired by mirroring vision.md everywhere
ruledOut.reason: Policy-driven by construction; Claude/Codex/Hermes mirror sets are already complete under the recorded exclusion rule

focus: Devin command surface: what the CLI loads, whether a command mirror is loadable, and the equivalent affordance
noveltyJustification: Answers the Devin command question at the mechanism level: the runtime's slash surface IS its skills surface, the retired mirror was skill-shaped at .devin/skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md, removal was an operator directive, and the goal hook was later restored while commands were not.
keyQuestions: What does the Devin CLI actually load as a command surface?
Is a Devin command mirror loadable at all, and in what shape?
What is the equivalent affordance and its cost?
answeredQuestions: What does the Devin CLI actually load as a command surface?
Is a Devin command mirror loadable at all, and in what shape?
What is the equivalent affordance and its cost?

ruledOut.approach: Treat the missing .devin/commands directory as an unclosed port to be closed by mirroring the 35 commands
ruledOut.reason: No loader exists for a commands tree; the retired mirror was skill-shaped at .devin/skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md and was removed on operator directive

focus: Skills surface: loader existence and correct-absence versus gap for Devin, Cursor and Codex; mirror shapes for Claude, Pi and Hermes
noveltyJustification: Supplies the mechanism behind each skills mirror plus the two cases the counts conceal: Hermes's 7 scanner-quarantined skills inside a generated mirror, and Cursor's compensating rules/skill-routing.md gap; also found a doc drift (.cursor/SYNC.md overcounts its command mirror by one) and a third unwired --check mode.
keyQuestions: Does each of Devin, Cursor and Codex have a skill loader?
Can the repo feed it?
Is the absence correct by nature or an unclosed gap?
answeredQuestions: Is the Cursor skills absence correct by nature? (yes, with an adjacent ungenerated packet list)
Is the Devin skills absence correct by nature? (yes, native discovery)
What shape must each skills mirror take? (symlink for Claude/Pi, generated markdown for Hermes)

ruledOut.reason: Cursor's skills directory is user-level and Cursor-managed; a repo mirror would not be read. The real gap is the ungenerated packet list in rules/skill-routing.md

focus: Goal parity across all seven runtimes: adapter, event wiring, identity source, and the cost of each partial path
noveltyJustification: Replaces the charter's adapter-directory framing with the hub's own seven-way classification, and finds the cell that framing would miss: Hermes has a working goal path the goal hub's table omits. Also new: injection-without-management performs a write, Cursor's limit is an identity limit, and neither Claude's nor Codex's manifest carries a breakable goal registration.
keyQuestions: How does a packet goal reach a session in each runtime?
Which runtimes have no path, and does each need an adapter, a native equivalent, or nothing?
What does a missing adapter cost mid-session?
answeredQuestions: How does a packet goal reach a session in each of the seven runtimes?
Which runtimes need an adapter? (none: Cursor's gap is identity, Claude/Codex are host-native)

ruledOut.approach: Recommend a goal-codex.md prompt stub as the primary Codex fix
ruledOut.reason: It builds around an unverified premise; the honest order is to probe the host path first and add the stub only if it fails

focus: Agents parity: in-sync vs merely present, the enforcing gate, its coverage, and observed drift
noveltyJustification: Turns the charter's presence claim into an observed gate verdict plus its exact comparison rule, and demonstrates a live blind spot: a semantic body rewrite survives a token-set gate because both words occur elsewhere in the document. Also finds the 12-vs-13 roster count, the two-upstream 'canonical' collision, and Pi as the only ungated generated agent tree.
keyQuestions: Are the agents mirrors in sync, not merely present?
Which gate keeps them in sync and does it cover every runtime?
Has any runtime's agent files drifted, and with what diff shape?
answeredQuestions: Are the agents mirrors in sync? (yes under the gate: 12 checked, all in sync, exit 0)
Which gate covers which runtime? (OpenCode-Claude pairs by check-agent-mirror-sync; Codex by sync-agents; Pi by nothing wired; symlink trees by link resolution)
Is there drift? (yes semantically in deep-research.md, invisible to the gate; no byte-level fork in the symlink trees)

ruledOut.approach: Recommend an agents content gate for Cursor, Devin or Hermes
ruledOut.reason: Their trees are symlinks; link resolution is the correct check and agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs already performs it

focus: Generator coverage: generated vs hand-maintained mirrors, --check existence, gate wiring, and drift already present
noveltyJustification: Highest-value iteration: it falsifies three manifest claims that the hook registration files are hand-authored and un-generatable, showing one registry and one gate-enforced generator produce all four; it concentrates the unwired checks on the two translation-heavy runtimes; and it counts the Cursor packet-list gap at 5 of 13.
keyQuestions: Which mirrors are generated and which hand-maintained?
Does each generated mirror have a --check mode wired into a gate that runs?
What drift is already present in hand-maintained surfaces, and what would a generator cost?
answeredQuestions: Which mirrors are generated vs hand-maintained?
Which --check modes are unwired? (four: pi agents, pi prompts, hermes prompts, hermes skills; plus sync-gate1-pointers pre-commit-only)
What drift is present in hand-maintained surfaces? (three instances, one with a counted 5-of-13 gap)

ruledOut.approach: Recommending a generator for .codex/config.toml or Pi's operator-state files
ruledOut.reason: The single-key merge rule has no clean TOML analogue at that size, and Pi's files are operator state rather than a derivation of a canonical repo source

focus: Hook parity: which concern packages reach which runtimes, which absences are by nature, and which are unported
noveltyJustification: Answers the hook question with a negative result that is itself the finding: no hook is unported, once Cursor's rule-file vision path and Pi's four-advisory bundle are accounted for. Also surfaces Pi's hand-authored guard layer as the one hook surface with no registry entry and no checker, and names the shared flag vocabulary as the mechanism that makes hook parity hold.
keyQuestions: Which hook packages reach which runtimes?
Which are runtime-specific by nature?
Which are simply unported?
How does this reconcile with the Hermes hook-parity work?
answeredQuestions: Which hook packages reach which runtimes? (20x6 matrix recorded)
Which are runtime-specific by nature? (four, already named by the Hermes work)
Which are unported? (none, after mechanism corrections)

ruledOut.approach: Recommending a Pi hook-drift checker as a parity fix
ruledOut.reason: The gap is a maintenance risk on a hand-authored layer, not a runtime missing a surface; it belongs in drift detection ranked on cost

focus: The Devin boundary: every repo-carriable surface Devin supports, every one it cannot, with proof per row
noveltyJustification: Enumerates the boundary with a config file, flag or live probe behind every row, and verifies the hook mirror is exactly complete (21/21 invoked scripts resolved, 0 broken). Load-bearing for any plan: the four-shape rule for reaching Devin, and the strict-YAML silent-drop as the cheapest broadly protective detector.
keyQuestions: What can .devin/ carry?
What can it not carry, and what proves each?
answeredQuestions: What can .devin/ carry? (agents, 8 hook events, MCP, skill-derived slash commands, prompts, vision, permission modes, subagents)
What can it not carry? (mirrored command tree, skills mirror, local rules dir, goal management)

ruledOut.approach: Treating Devin's zero-command surface as parity debt to be paid
ruledOut.reason: Both the runtime (no loader) and an operator directive place the boundary; the honest row is 'cannot carry'

focus: Drift detection: single gate or partial gates, their blind spots, and the cheapest detector for the Devin command class
noveltyJustification: Answers 'is there a single gate' with no, and inverts the assumption: the manual /doctor route covers more than either automated gate. Names the structural gap (every checker asks equality, none asks surface existence), observes the catalog checker confirming 35 commands, and locates the exemption registry that already exists but is wired to generators instead of a coverage assertion.
keyQuestions: Is there a single gate that would notice any runtime falling behind?
What are each partial gate's blind spots?
What is the cheapest detector for the Devin command class and its per-commit cost?
answeredQuestions: Is there a single gate? (no: four automated entry points plus one manual route)
What are the blind spots? (equality-vs-existence, token-set equality, change-scoped execution, four unwired --check modes, no strict-YAML checker)
What is the cheapest detector? (a surface-coverage assertion table, generalizing agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs)

ruledOut.reason: A similarity score would either fire constantly or miss the case; the control is a review step

focus: Synthesis: ranked recommendations, the five charter deliverables, and the phase decomposition
noveltyJustification: Converts nine iterations of evidence into decisions; the novel observation is that R1-R7 are all list and text edits with no new mechanism, and that the only new code worth writing is R3 (strict frontmatter parse) and R4 (coverage table plus walk), both of which have an existing in-repo pattern.
keyQuestions: What is the ranked recommendation list?
What is the phase decomposition?
answeredQuestions: Ranked recommendation list? (R1-R7 do now, R8-R12 do next, D1-D7 do not)
Phase decomposition? (P1-P6 with dependencies and closing gates)

convergenceNote: Convergence before the cap is telemetry only in this lineage; the ratio trail never breached 0.05 and iteration 10 is an explicit synthesis pass, so no early STOP was taken.
questionsAnswered: 10/10 angle questions closed; 6 sub-questions recorded as open with their confirming checks
